analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (27.10.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 70bps to 7677 (+12% YTD) on low volumes with signs of AI stabilisation. SOX gained 2.8%, optical networks +4% and defense spending +3% led. Bovespa closed -14% after Lula's election. Kospi +3% on SK Hynix +5% and Samsung +4%.
Levels cited: US 10-year at 4.97%, Brent $115 with no de-escalation, Gold $4009, Bitcoin $80k.

Fed meeting is the next day. GS expects the FOMC to skip raising rates and likely deliver a second hike in December. The key question is how the statement modifies the sentence referring to the September hike. No significant new information expected from the press conference.
Broadcom, SpaceX and Meta fundraising announcements add up to another $198bn, showing the scale of capital needed for the AI build-out.

Rates vs growth: large deficits, AI-linked borrowing and central bank hikes have raised yields by an average of about 100bp across DM curves since early 2026. If sustained, GS estimates a cumulative 0.6% subtraction from GDP via housing, consumer durables and business investment.

Tech is an increasingly important driver of risk appetite. The correlation between GS's risk appetite indicator and Nasdaq 100 performance relative to S&P 500 equal weight reached almost 1 in the most recent week.

Central bankers increasingly cite the AI buildout as an inflation driver. GS sees three channels: higher memory prices passing to consumer prices, spillover from memory prices to consumer electronics, and higher electricity prices from data center power demand. GS considers the direct and indirect pressures limited.
Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60k employees (25% of its global workforce) and laid off about 15k workers last year.

China: GS estimates high-tech sectors contributed roughly 2% a year to real GDP growth in 2016-25 and expects about 2% a year in 2026-30. High-tech is 23% of GDP in 2026 vs 15% for property. Data center build-out is a key part of the 'Six Networks' investment initiative.

Idea: buy the dip in Greek banks (GSXEGRBK). The basket pulled back about 15%, close to oversold. Domestic balance sheets are the healthiest in over a decade, and EPS growth and EPS revision breadth are close to a 5-year high.
CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures, in the 91st percentile historically and nearly 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked. Positioning now matters more for the left tail.
Prediction markets are a fast-growing retail alternative. Monthly volumes grew to $78bn in Sep26 from $5bn a year earlier.
CoreWeave: after the recent upgrade, the analyst team spoke to more than 100 investors. The key message is that the company does not need unsecured debt, a market described as basically closed.

Kospi target cut from 12k to 9k to reflect more conservative assumptions about how the market prices fundamentals. GS still sees attractive risk/reward. The 9k target implies 6.5x consensus forward P/E and 1.5x P/B vs 23% ROE.
Stat of the Day: the top 10% of households by wealth own 87% of total household equity assets, so US household equity demand is closely tied to the behavior of wealthy investors.
Chart of the Day: higher bond yields are likely to weigh on global growth. Earnings in focus: SK Hynix, Alphabet and Microsoft the next day, Samsung, Amazon and Intel on Thursday.
